title: Browser-engine clients connect from any origin, without credentials
description: Fluster (a Tauri WebView) and any web client hosted on another origin fail before sign-in: API answers carry no Access-Control-Allow-Origin and preflights answer 404 (issue #202). D-016: open to any origin, never with credentials; tokens travel only in headers or the query, so no other site can make a viewer's browser send one.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed first: a rerunnable capture in compat/captures of a real Jellyfin 12.4 records the status and every Access-Control-*, Vary and Allow header it answers, for two different origins and for no Origin, to: a GET of an open route; a GET of a viewer route with a token and with none; a ranged GET of a film; a preflight for the sign-in (POST, asking authorization and content-type); a preflight asking range; one asking DELETE and one asking PATCH; one asking a header outside the six below; and a GET and a preflight for an unserved path

Every difference between that capture and what jellyscale answers to the same requests (status, Access-Control-*, Vary) is in compat/differences.yaml with its reason, and a check asks jellyscale the capture's requests and fails on a difference that is not listed

In Chromium, a page served from an origin other than the server's reads GET /System/Info/Public, reads a wrong password as a 401 (not as a failed connection), signs in with POST /Users/AuthenticateByName (JSON body), and lists the libraries and one library's films, sending Authorization: MediaBrowser on every request and its token in no URL; the server is two api replicas and a stream replica as separate processes behind the router, and each of these requests is answered by an api replica

The same page, its token still only in the Authorization header, direct plays a film from bytes it fetched by script: a request for a range in the middle of the file answers 206 with exactly those bytes, the page itself reads Content-Range, Accept-Ranges and Content-Length from the answer, and the picture advances before and after a seek; the stream replica answers each request and its preflight

The same page plays a film that transcodes, sending the Authorization header on the master playlist, the main playlist and every segment (ApiKey taken off the TranscodingUrl): time advances, and after a seek beyond what was buffered a segment at the new place is fetched and time advances there; the stream replica answers each request and its preflight
Each of those steps is shown to fail on today's build by itself: the open read, the sign-in, and, given a token obtained outside the page, the browse, the direct play and the transcode

Each of the 92 routes of compat/endpoints.yaml (the 4 under /jellyscale/v1/ and GET /socket included), asked on a process that has only the route's role (79 on api alone, 13 on stream alone), answers a preflight from each of tauri://localhost, http://tauri.localhost, https://tauri.localhost and an https web origin, 368 in all, with a 2xx that allows that origin, the route's method and all six of Authorization, X-Emby-Authorization, X-Emby-Token, X-MediaBrowser-Token, Content-Type and Range; a path in another letter case or with a trailing slash is answered as the route itself is, checked on every route of compat/endpoints.yaml, not one (D-019)

Each of the six headers is allowed when asked alone, together, in any order and in any letter case, and Authorization is allowed by name (a browser does not take `*` for it); the 5 DELETE and 2 PATCH routes are allowed by name, each of the 8 paths with two methods allows both, HEAD is allowed wherever GET is served, and a path in another letter case or with a trailing slash is answered as the route itself is

Every answer of a route to a request that carries an Origin allows that origin, whatever the answer: 200, 204, 206, the 401 of no token, an unknown token and a wrong password, a handler's 404, a 416, and a 5xx from a store failure; the query spellings (ApiKey, api_key) need no preflight and their answers are readable the same way

A picture asked from one origin, from another and with no Origin is right for each from a shared cache: the allowed origin is `*`, or every answer of the route, with an Origin or without, carries Vary: Origin

Wherever an answer carries Content-Range or Accept-Ranges (the direct play, the download and the subtitle and font files, on 200, 206 and HEAD), a page on another origin can read them and Content-Length

A preflight needs no token and no Postgres: it is answered the same with no credential, a valid token and an unknown one, for an id that exists and one that does not, by a server with no database, and, on an api replica and on a stream replica, while Postgres is stopped (answered before Postgres returns, having sent it no statement); a viewer in the snapshot who plays from another origin with a header token still gets each segment or range and its preflight, with the origin allowed, through the outage

A preflight carries no information about the server and does nothing: no body, no header whose value differs between two servers (name, id, version) or with what the database holds, no handler run (a preflight for POST /Sessions/Logout or DELETE /Videos/ActiveEncodings changes nothing, even with a token on it), and one for a served route is not logged as an unknown route

Nothing an operator owns is opened: a GET with an Origin and a preflight for /healthz and for /readyz (ready, and 503) on an api and on a stream process, and for /metrics on the metrics listener of an api, a stream and a worker process, carry no Access-Control-* header, and answer the status and body they answer today
No answer carries Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: none of the 368 preflights, no answer of the 92 routes with a token or without, no error answer, and none to a request that sends a Cookie header

A check driven from the route table (so a new route is covered) fails if any route's answer, with a token, without one, or to a preflight, carries Set-Cookie, and a valid token sent only in a Cookie header, under each spelling's name, is answered 401 `unauthorized`; the check is shown to fail on a build that sets a cookie
DOMAINS.md has an invariant that a viewer's token never travels in a cookie and no route sets one, naming that check and binding JS-039 and JS-122 by name
No route's access changes: the open list is the same 11 routes, and each of the 81 viewer routes asked from another origin with no token still answers 401 `unauthorized`

jellyfin-web served by jellyscale and the differential tier's clients get the status, the body and every header other than Access-Control-* and Vary that they got before; the browse, play, subtitles, failover and transcode gates and the differential tier pass with no existing scenario, request or allowlist entry changed

docs/access.md says a preflight is open to anyone and why (a browser sends it with no token, before any request that carries one in a header), that any origin may call the API and media routes, why that does not open a viewer's account (no cookie: a page can only use a token it already holds), what it does expose (on a server reachable only on a private network, a web page in a viewer's browser can read the open routes and the result of a sign-in attempt), and that /healthz, /readyz and /metrics are not opened; its sentence that every other method and path gets the catch-all's 404 is made true again
docs/status.md's Fluster row says what was shown (Chromium on another origin; preflights for the three WebView origins) and that Fluster itself has not been run, naming JS-075 (D-019)
notes: D-019: the Fluster record moved to JS-075; shipped on Chromium cross-origin and preflight evidence.
